summary: Happy Eyeballs chooses IPv6 egress through branch proxy that rewrites SNI, causing intermittent artifact TLS certname mismatch in private deploy
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart is seeing intermittent model artifact fetch failures from serving nodes in their private deployment. Failures manifest as TLS certificate name mismatch (x509: certificate is valid for storage.internal.corp, not artifacts.s3-external.net) when nodes attempt to download shard objects. This happens ~0.3-0.8% of shard fetches, spikes during nightly warmups.

Impact: Inference requests occasionally return 502/5xx or experience longer tail latency while retries happen. Customer reports degraded end-user batch jobs during peak.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peering to our control plane) with egress routed through the customer's branch-office proxy/NGFW. Serving nodes are dual-stack (IPv4+IPv6) and use system default Happy Eyeballs behavior.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger model rollout that causes serving nodes to fetch shard objects concurrently (large model or batch warmup).
2) Observe artifact fetch logs and TLS errors on a subset of nodes.
3) Failures correlate with a resolver returning AAAA records and the kernel selecting IPv6 egress first.

Logs / observations:
- serving-node.log: "GET https://artifacts.s3-external.net/model-12345/shard-0: x509: certificate is valid for storage.internal.corp, not artifacts.s3-external.net"
- tcpdump on node during failure shows TLS ClientHello SNI = "artifacts.s3-external.net" but proxy/NGFW upstream opens TLS to storage.internal.corp endpoint (IPv6 path) and responds with a different certificate.
- DNS responses during failure include AAAA then A; Happy Eyeballs chooses IPv6 path leading to branch proxy path.

Suspected cause: Branch-office egress path for IPv6 is hairpinned through an intermediate corporate proxy that performs SNI rewriting (or routes to an internal storage translator) only for IPv6-preferring flows. IPv4 egress takes a different ISP path that preserves SNI. Happy Eyeballs/dual-stack behavior causes a fraction of connections to use IPv6 and encounter proxy SNI rewrite, producing hostname mismatch.

Temporary workaround: Request customer to either (a) prefer IPv4 on serving nodes (gai.conf / sysctl tweak) or (b) add an exception in the branch proxy to preserve SNI for artifacts.s3-external.net/storage endpoints. We provided exact gai.conf line to prefer IPv4.

Requested next steps:
- Collect pcap and proxy logs from customer for a failing window.
- Confirm proxy rule that rewrites SNI or routes IPv6 traffic differently.
- Consider adding an artifact fetch fallback that retries with IPv4 on TLS hostname mismatch to avoid transient failures.
workarounds: 1) Customer applied temporary gai.conf preference to prefer IPv4 on serving nodes (precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100). 2) Customer created an exception in branch proxy to stop SNI rewrite for artifacts.s3-external.net. Both reduced failure rate to <0.01% during tests.
investigation_notes:
- 2026-03-12 09:10 Support triage: Identified x509 certname mismatch errors in serving logs; customer confirmed private egress via branch proxy.
- 2026-03-12 11:45 SRE captured tcpdump showing ClientHello->proxy->upstream change only on AAAA path.
- 2026-03-13 14:20 Eng hypothesis: proxy rewrites destination or uses different backend for IPv6 egress (NAT64 or internal cache) leading to certificate for internal hostname.
- Gathered artifacts: pcap (redacted), serving logs, DNS query/response samples, proxy ACL snippet from customer (sensitive - stored in secure ticket file).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied: customer prefers IPv4 on nodes; proxy exception configured. Root cause: asymmetric egress behavior where IPv6 flows were routed through a proxy path that replaced or proxied TLS to an internal storage hostname, causing x509 name mismatch. Permanent recommendation: customer to update proxy to preserve SNI for public artifact hostnames or ensure consistent egress routing for IPv6 and IPv4. We will add a robustness change to the artifact fetcher to attempt IPv4 fallback on TLS hostname mismatch (tracked in INT-8893).
resolution: Workarounds implemented by customer reduced errors to noise level. Engineering task created (INT-8893) to add lightweight IPv4 fallback when artifact fetch fails with certname mismatch. Support to follow up in 2 weeks to confirm stability.
